beats.say: Why does the casino always win at roulette? Look at this one green pocket.
beats.cap: Why does the casino|always win at roulette?|Look at this|one green pocket.

beats.say: A European wheel has thirty seven pockets: the numbers one to thirty six, plus a single zero.
beats.cap: A European wheel|has 37 pockets:|the numbers 1 to 36,|plus a single zero.

beats.say: Put a chip on one number and win, and the casino pays you thirty five to one.
beats.cap: Put a chip on one number|and win, and the casino|pays you 35 to 1.

beats.say: But with thirty seven pockets, a fair payout would be thirty six to one.
beats.cap: But with 37 pockets,|a fair payout would be|36 to 1.

beats.say: That one missing chip on every win is where the casino's edge comes from.
beats.cap: That one missing chip|on every win is where|the casino's edge comes from.

beats.say: It works out to a house edge of about two point seven percent on every bet.
beats.cap: It works out to|a house edge of about|2.7% on every bet.

beats.say: Bet ten dollars a spin for a thousand spins, and you can expect to lose about two hundred seventy dollars.
beats.cap: Bet $10 a spin|for 1,000 spins,|and you can expect|to lose about $270.

beats.say: American wheels add a second green pocket, the double zero, and the edge almost doubles to five point two six percent.
beats.cap: American wheels add|a second green pocket,|the double zero, and the edge|almost doubles to 5.26%.

beats.say: So the next time you lose at roulette, you were not unlucky.
beats.cap: So the next time|you lose at roulette,|you were not unlucky.

beats.say: You were playing against the zero.
